_comment: Launch parameters in two layers. 'policy' does not depend on the model or the platform: how the server is driven — the app owns it, and the settings UI does not show it. 'profiles' is the platform layer, keyed by os+backend, and it owns what belongs to the machine — the three hardware parameters (n-gpu-layers, flash-attn, ctx-size) — and it is the only layer the settings table shows and the user edits. Everything else lives in models/<id>.json: what the weights need (spec decoding, image-*-tokens, special) the machine cannot decide, and the request profile carries max_tokens per role. A user copy of a platform profile that carries any other name is dropped at startup.

parameters.name: parallel
parameters.description: Number of concurrent server slots.

parameters.name: cache-reuse
parameters.description: Context reuse window between requests; 0 disables.

parameters.name: no-context-shift
parameters.description: Keep the context stable: do not shift the KV cache when the window overflows.

parameters.name: no-warmup
parameters.description: Skip the warmup run at model load (faster start, slower first request).

parameters.name: n-gpu-layers
parameters.description: Number of model layers offloaded to the GPU; 99 = all.

parameters.name: flash-attn
parameters.description: Flash attention: on, off or auto.

parameters.name: ctx-size
parameters.description: Model context window in tokens (prompt + image + output). The machine's memory decides this — lower it if a page comes out truncated.
